frontier.hypothesis: Class C closes on the target's A-first store order by moving the SHORT quantity into the chain's interval rather than moving the chain: the chain occupies [26,56] and the reload [48,52] in every A-first build, so any 4-ref, 2-unit throwaway quantity born in (26,48) satisfies containment.
frontier.mechanism: block_alloc allocates in qty_order; a 4-ref/2-unit quantity has priority 4.0 and is allocated before the 22-ref chain (3.14), taking $2. If its interval sits inside the chain's, $2 is still busy when the chain is allocated, the chain falls to $3, and the reload -- born at 48, after the short quantity died -- finds $2. Today's short quantity is born at 12, two units before the chain starts.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate ordinary-C forms that create a short-lived throwaway value in the MIDDLE of the store block rather than before it: the S-group address (base + t0) computed into a named local declared between the D and C groups; the &D_800A35D0 symbol address named in its own local so its lui/addiu pair forms a 4-ref quantity after the chain root's birth; a named local for the group-A pointer reused for a later group. Run tmp/grind/func_800770B8/s26/qty.sh on each and ACCEPT ONLY variants whose block-1 table shows a refs<=4 quantity with birth > 26 and death < 48 -- score only those. This is one cc1 run per candidate, so the sweep is cheap.

frontier.hypothesis: There is a store-order perturbation strictly weaker than fCADS that starts the chain quantity at 12 while leaving group A's five stores emitted first, i.e. buys containment without fCADS's 15-row price.
frontier.mechanism: fCADS buys chain birth 12 by putting group C first, and its whole 12-point cost is confined to rows 40-54 (measured this session). The s23 sweep permuted WHOLE groups only; splitting a group's address computation from its stores was never tried, and sched1 sinks the t0*4 sll to its first consumer -- which can be a pointer computation whose stores stay put.
frontier.next_probe: Build the split-group shapes on the flipped cursor: (a) C's pointer computed first with C's stores left after D; (b) D's lui/addiu/addu first with D's stores after A; (c) both. Read the block-1 qty table for chain birth 12 AND a refs<=4 quantity fully inside [12,48] before scoring. Note s26 proved a named-pointer LOCAL does not do this on its own (d1/d2/d3 all keep birth 26-28), so the address computation must acquire a consumer that forces sched1 to place it early, not merely a name.

frontier.hypothesis: The C-level difference that makes the floor body's 0x5C site satisfy the containment criterion (sum quantity [4,26] containing short [8,12], reload [16,20] taking $2) can be transplanted onto the cursor site, closing class C with no flip and no store reorder.
frontier.mechanism: Both sites compile from base-first C to identical RTL, and block 3 of the FLOOR body already produces exactly the interval nesting the cursor site needs. The geometric difference is that at the 0x5C site the sum quantity is born at 4 -- at the top of its block -- whereas at the cursor site it is born at 26-28, after the whole store block.
frontier.next_probe: Diff block 1 and block 3 of s26/F.qty and the corresponding .lreg insn streams to identify which pseudo is born at 4 in block 3 and why the tie fires there, then look for the C construct that reproduces it in block 1. Concretely: block 3's t0*2 shift feeds both the sp[t0] address (addu $a1,$v1,$t3 at target row 89) and the 0x5C base, i.e. the shift has a SECOND consumer that is not the add -- the cursor's t0*10 shift has only one. Test whether giving the cursor's shift a second real consumer (a value the target also computes) moves the sum quantity's birth to the shift.

judge_constraints: func_800770B8's honest floor stays 5. Do not respell the t0*4->t0*2 identity detour in any form. The dependence may only be reached if it is FORCED by real program structure -- e.g. group A addressed through a cursor genuinely derived from group C's t0*4 pointer, where the derivation has a truthful semantic reading and emits no instruction the target lacks.
